dct_description_sm: Note: *The focus of the Igliniit Project is on developing a new technology to collect data.  All data collected in the project is test data at this time and not available.* The Igliniit Project brings together geomatics engineers and Inuit hunters to design a new, integrated field computer, GPS system, and mobile weather station that can be easily and affordably mounted on snow machines, dog teams and other modes of travel used by Inuit hunters in Canada who log thousands of kilometres per year. The system automatically logs the location of the snow machine/sled/observer every thirty seconds, providing geo-referenced waypoints that can later be mapped to produce the traveller's routes.  In addition to tracking routes, the Igliniit system logs weather conditions (temperature, humidity, pressure, etc.) and the observations of hunters (e.g. animals, sea ice features, hazards, placenames) through a customized computer touchscreen that has a user-friendly icon interface available in English or Inuktitut.  Digital cameras (photo and video) that the hunters carry with them provide visual images at certain waypoints.
